items.title: Alvin Queen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: It’s like Billie Holiday records have sold more since she’s died then since she was alive, and it’s history.

ctx.x: “So What” — Miles Davis, this kid in London did this thing “So What” with a back beat, it’s making money. I mean, then they took, let me see, one of the Latin bands, they took something of Monk’s and they did a Latin version of it. So it’s really hard to say. It’s like Latin music, and then they say “salsa” music. We’re back in the commercial market, we’re back in it again. I don’t care how you turn it around, anything that makes money is

commercial form. Jazz has never made any really big money. Jazz lives for a period of time. It’s like Billie Holiday records have sold more since she’s died then since she was alive, and it’s history. When you want to go hear a trumpet player, and you go buy Sweets and you buy Clark Terry, then you hear — I want to learn the trumpet, you see? So the jazz lives on but I mean hip hop and bebop, and you know as Roy Haynes would say, Roy would say, “My picture’s not in there, my name’s not there.”
So you have been a resident of Switzerland for how long now?
